next_step: Finalize committed GPU hours and burst policy; legal to review SOW
company_description: Mid-market B2B SaaS maker of a modular user engagement platform (in-app guidance + chat + insights). Heavy downstream ML pipelines, product teams building AI-driven assistants for onboarding and contextual help.
notes: Overview: Eng team of ~45 (ML+infra) evaluating Redwood for inference tier. Primary path: start with Hosted API POC -> move to Dedicated with reserved GPU pools after SLA + cost analysis.
Quote from VP Product: 'We need predictable unit economics. If we can nail committed throughput + burst, we'll consolidate vendors.'

POC objectives: validate p95 latency <200ms for chat at 8 concurrent users per shard; embeddings throughput 120 qps; reranking latency budget 80ms internal call. Quantization-friendly models preferred (FP16/4-bit).
Security: must support SSO/SAML, KMS for key management, SOC2 compliance, audit logs, option for US-only data residency. Legal flagged DPA clauses (data-retention + subprocessors).

Pricing ask: want 12-month committed plan with monthly ramp schedule, predictable overage formula (prefer per-token at x1.5 of committed rate), and explicit burst pools (up to 2x committed for 72 hours) with transparent throttling behavior.
Capacity preference: H100-class or equivalent for latency-sensitive chat; fallback to A10G for embeddings/reranking. Interested in autoscaling + burst credits for seasonal spikes.
Technical win from demo: Redwood streaming + KV cache reduced end-to-end tokens by ~18% in our sample flows. SE demo recording: ff_20250218_zenithway_demo.

Pricing friction: internal finance wants line-item showing committed GPU hours, included burst hours, expected overage dollars at +25% traffic, and clear ramp schedule (month 1: 10% commit; month 3: 40%; month 6: 100%).
Competitive note: evaluated Anthropic (good quality) but costs for dedicated setup and lack of routing controls were concerns; OpenAI cheaper for hosted but no private/dedicated option they like.

Requested deliverables from Redwood: 1) sample SOW with commit tiers (monthly GPU-hour blocks), 2) clear overage formula and example invoice, 3) runbook for failover to hosted model variant, 4) security questionnaire answers (sent to drive link).
